Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

<system-reminder>
The following MCP servers require authentication before their tools can be used:
plugin:exa:exa

Claude cannot start the OAuth flow itself. If the user's request depends on one of these servers (even if they didn't name it explicitly), or they ask about it, tell them that it needs to be authorized — for claude.ai connectors, via their claude.ai connector settings; for other servers, via /mcp — and that the capability is unavailable until they do. Otherwise carry on with the request and do not mention these servers. Do not ask the user for authorization codes, tokens, or callback URLs.
</system-reminder>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- role-play-vibing:coder: Исполнитель кода: пишет или правит код проекта (любой язык, скрипты) по поручению роли. Использовать для любой части задачи, где меняется код. (Tools: All tools)

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. **Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. The menu bar does not, as long as the app that is frontmost is one you already have access to.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

**Splash screen rule:** The page doesn't state a restriction. It says "you can customize your splash screen to present projects the way you or your clients desire."

**Runtime fee:** The page doesn't mention one. It links to a separate pricing-updates page for more information.

**Conditions that require Pro or a subscription:**
- **Revenue or funding above the threshold:** The page says that if revenue or funds raised exceed $200K in the last 12 months, you should "choose one of our subscription plans."
- **Closed platforms (Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, Xbox):** Building and deploying to these requires "an active Unity Pro subscription," or a "Preferred Platform license key" from the platform holder. You also need approval from each platform holder.

**License:** MIT. The page says "License: MIT — see LICENSE."

**Latest release:** v10.3.0, dated 2026-10-04.

**Last commit date:** Not shown. The page lists 2,026 commits but no date for the latest one.

**Stars:** 15.3k.

**Tools and capabilities:** The page cites "50 focused MCP tool entrypoints" and says the tools can:
- Create scenes and GameObjects
- Edit C# scripts
- Manage assets
- Run tests
- Profile
- Build

The page links to a full tool catalog. It does not explicitly mention console access, screenshots, or play mode.

**Supported OS:** Windows is not mentioned.

**Requirements:**
- Unity 2021.3 LTS through 6.x
- Python 3.10+, installed via `uv`

**Connecting to Claude Code:** The page says the project works with "Claude Desktop & Code" and other MCP clients. Setup is through Unity's `Window → MCP for Unity → Configure All Detected Clients`. No Claude Code-specific steps are given.

**Paid components:** None for MCP for Unity, which is free and MIT-licensed. The page separately promotes Aura for Unity as a premium product from the same maintainers, but it is not part of this project.

**Runtime Fee:** Canceled. Unity announced the cancellation on September 12, 2024, and it took effect immediately. It does not apply to games made with Unity 6 or any other version. Unity states that no games were ever subject to it because it was never implemented.

**Unity Personal revenue limit:** Up to $200,000 in annual revenue and funding. The increased threshold ($0 to $200,000 USD) took effect with the Unity 6 release on October 17, 2024. Businesses above $200K need Unity Pro.

**Splash screen:** Optional with Unity 6, listed as available now for the Personal plan.

**2026 changes:**
- **Pro and Enterprise pricing:** A 5% increase starts January 12, 2026. Existing subscribers see the new price at their first renewal on or after that date.
- **Havok Physics:** Starting with Unity 6.3, Havok Physics is no longer included with Pro, Enterprise, or Industry. Support continues for Unity 2022 LTS and 6.0 LTS for the rest of their lifecycles. Requests now go to Microsoft's Havok team.
- **DevOps (Version Control and Build Automation):** Changes are scheduled to take effect March 1, 2026. They include:
  - Removal of public cloud seat charges for Unity Version Control.
  - Free storage raised from 5 GB to 25 GB per org per month.
  - 100 GB of free egress per month. Egress is not charged in March or April 2026.
  - Additional free build minutes, including 100 Mac minutes and 100 Linux minutes.
  - Editor concurrency increased from 1 to 2.
- **Later in 2026:** All plans are set to gain expanded free DevOps access. Personal remains free in 2026.

**Unity-MCP (IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP): Extracted Details**

- **License:** Apache-2.0.
- **Latest release version and date:** Not stated. The Releases section is empty in the captured content.
- **Last commit date:** Not stated. The page shows 3,174 commits but no date.
- **Stars:** 4.5k. Forks: 401. Watchers: 29.

**Tools and capabilities**
- **Scenes:** create, open, save, unload, set active, list opened, and get scene data.
- **GameObjects:** create, find, modify, duplicate, destroy, set parent, and manage components.
- **Tests:** `tests-run` executes EditMode and PlayMode Unity tests.
- **Console:** get logs with filtering, and clear logs.
- **Screenshots:** game view, scene view, camera, and isolated GameObject renders.
- **Play mode:** get and set editor state (start, stop, pause).
- **Other:** 70+ built-in tools, including asset management, Roslyn-based script execution, and reflection-based method calls. Optional extensions cover Animation, Cinemachine, Input System, Navigation, Particle System, ProBuilder, Splines, Terrain, Tilemap, and Timeline.

**Supported OS**
- The page lists Windows (x64, x86, arm64), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), and Linux (x64, arm64) server binaries. It notes that Docker Desktop must be running on Windows.

**Requirements**
- The Unity project path cannot contain spaces.
- An AI agent that supports Skills or dynamic MCP tool updates.
- Node/npm for the CLI (`npm install -g unity-mcp-cli`), or the `.unitypackage` installer as an alternative.
- Docker is optional, for containerized deployment.

**Unity version requirements**
- Not specified. The badges read "Editor-X" and "Runtime-X" without version numbers.

**Connecting to Claude Code**
- Option 1: Open `Window/AI Game Developer` in Unity and click "Auto-generate skills" (recommended).
- Option 2: Run `npx unity-mcp-cli setup-skills claude-code ./MyUnityProject`.
- Option 3: Add the server manually with `claude mcp add ai-game-developer <command>`, where `<command>` is the platform-specific server path plus `port=<port>` and `client-transport=stdio`.

**Paid components**
- The project describes itself as free. The page names no paid components.

content.content:
**What it is:** The Unity CLI is a terminal-native way to connect agents, CI pipelines, and custom tools to Unity. The post calls it "our recommended path forward" for new users, and says the existing Unity MCP remains supported.

**What it can do (per the page):**
- **Run C#:** `unity eval` runs arbitrary C# through the Roslyn compiler, avoiding long compilation times and domain reloads.
- **Run commands:** `unity command` runs built-in or custom Editor commands. You can write custom commands to give agents project-specific context.
- **Runtime access:** It can drive development builds for live debugging, game-state changes, and automated playtesting.
- **MCP Mode:** `unity mcp --help` exposes setup commands for existing MCP-based agents. You don't need the separate Unity MCP first.
- **CI:** The post describes installing the correct Editor, running headless Editor and Player tests, and reporting results.
- **Multiple Editors:** It can communicate with several Editors.

**Not confirmed on the page:** Screenshots, builds, and console access aren't explicitly listed. Profiler and Frame Debugger integrations are planned before general availability, and shader graph support was requested but not mentioned.

**Cost:** The post says "we are making these tools free," covering both the CLI and MCP, with no concurrency limits on the MCP server. It doesn't mention a Personal license or any license requirement, so I can't confirm what licensing applies.

**Installation:** A staff reply says it's available through the package manager and points to the blog and documentation for setup. No Windows-specific steps are given. One user running it from a JetBrains Rider AI chat with Codex hit a `mkdir` EEXIST error on the UnityHub logs folder. Running the same `unity.exe --help` command through PowerShell worked for them.

**Agent use (e.g., Claude Code):** The post says you can bring your own agent, naming Claude, Codex, Copilot, and local models. It doesn't describe Claude Code setup specifically. Official reusable skills for coding agents are in a GitHub repository (Unity-Technologies/skills).

**Limitations:**
- It's pre-GA. Related topics reference beta releases.
- Profiler and Frame Debugger integrations aren't yet available.
- The Windows issue above was reported by one user, not confirmed by Unity.

**What ships today (0.1.0 beta)**
- **Standalone CLI:** Covers Editor installs, module listing, project opening, authentication, licensing, Unity Cloud, project cloning, and a `unity doctor` diagnostic.
- **`com.unity.pipeline` (experimental):** Lets a running Editor accept CLI commands. Any static method marked with `[CliCommand]` is discovered automatically. Requires Unity 6.0 LTS or newer.
- **`unity eval`:** Compiles and runs a C# expression inside a running Editor, gated by a security token.
- **Built-in MCP:** `unity mcp` provides an MCP mode, so the older Unity MCP is not required.
- **CI commands:** `unity test` returns exit code 6 when tests run and fail. `unity build` handles Android signing and derives versions from Git tags.

**Windows support**
Windows is covered by a PowerShell install script that uses the beta channel. Homebrew, winget, and apt support is planned but not shipped. Prebuilt binaries via GitHub Releases are waiting on internal approvals. The article does not describe other Windows-specific limitations.

**What's still broken**
- **Token bug:** Entering Play Mode regenerates the Pipeline server's bearer token. MCP clients that cached the old token get 401 errors until they restart. Unity says a fix ships the week of the post.
- **Editor focus and dialogs:** The Editor sometimes needs foreground focus to refresh assets or reload the domain. Modal dialogs can block agents. The suggested workaround is launching with `-automated`.
- **Performance:** One developer measured about 0.80 seconds per call versus 0.05 seconds for their internal tooling, roughly 16 times slower. They also reported poor token efficiency and missing operations, such as reordering hierarchy objects.
- **Discoverability:** The CLI gives agents no tool list, so a `unity-cli` skill or an AGENTS.md file is needed.
- **Missing features:** Profiler and frame debugger integrations are planned but not yet included.

**License requirements**
The article mentions floating and offline activation, floating license servers, and service-account authentication through environment variables for headless agents. Unity's engineers said the MCP is free with unlimited concurrent connections on the latest version. The article does not specify which license tier is required for each feature.

**Personal edition**
The article does not mention the Personal edition.

**Commands**
- **Screenshot:** Not mentioned. The article's screenshot reference concerns Unity AI's Scene View snapshots, not the CLI.
- **Test:** `unity test` runs Edit Mode and Play Mode tests in batch mode and writes NUnit XML output.
- **Build:** `unity build` exports APK, AAB, or Android Studio projects.
- **Exec C#:** `unity eval` runs an expression in a running Editor. `eval_file` handles longer scripts, and `--runtime` targets a live Player. The announcement uses `unity command eval`, while the release notes use `unity eval`. The article advises checking `unity --help` on your installed version.

**Comparison to MCP bridges**
- **Community MCP servers:** Teams previously had to build and maintain their own Editor bridge. The article calls these a maintenance liability, and they were prone to breaking on domain reloads.
- **Built-in CLI MCP:** Unity's engineers say it performs better on focus handling, domain reloads, and managing multiple Editors.
- **Tailored MCP layer:** The article's recommendation is a custom MCP server built on the CLI. It would expose only the operations a pipeline needs, return compact results, and reduce latency and token use compared with a generic tool surface.

The page content includes only one full release, **1.0.0-beta.14 (October 21, 2026)**. The rest of the notes are truncated, so I can't cover the last 3–4 releases. The notes also don't mention "Personal" or "machine mode" by name. Here is what 1.0.0-beta.14 says about your other topics.

## 1.0.0-beta.14 (October 21, 2026)

### Windows
- The machine-wide `services-config.json` is used only if the file and every folder above it can be changed only by Administrators, SYSTEM, or TrustedInstaller. Otherwise the CLI uses default licensing settings.
- The MSIX (winget) package now requires Windows 10 version 21H1 or later.
- `unity uninstall`, `unity editors prune --remove`, and `unity editors upgrade --replace` remove Editors you own without asking for admin rights. Other Editors get one administrator prompt per command. Setting `UNITY_NO_ELEVATE` refuses the removal instead.
- `unity build run` no longer passes your service-account secret or source-host tokens to the player it starts.
- `unity open` and `unity projects open` now report the real Editor process ID in `launchedPid`. It was always `0` before.
- A system proxy set only for HTTP is no longer used for `https://` requests.
- Plugins installed from the MSIX package on Windows 11 are visible to other CLI installs and to Unity Hub.

### Licensing
- `unity license activate` reads `UNITY_LICENSE_SERIAL` when you pass no `--serial` or other activation option, which keeps the serial out of the process list:
  ```
  export UNITY_LICENSE_SERIAL=<your-serial>
  unity license activate
  ```
- A perpetual or legacy serial license needs no sign-in: `unity license activate --serial <serial>`. A subscription serial still requires a signed-in user.
- `unity license status` with no active license now reports `success: false` with `LICENSE_NOT_ACTIVE` in JSON. `unity license server status` reports `LICENSE_SERVER_NOT_CONFIGURED` or `LICENSE_SERVER_UNREACHABLE` in the same way. Exit codes and `data` are unchanged.
- The CLI now uses Unity Licensing Client 1.19.0. An older downloaded client is replaced the next time a `unity license` command or an Editor launch needs it.

### Personal
- Not mentioned.

### Machine mode
- Not mentioned by name. The closest items are unattended-run options:
  - `unity open --accept-upgrades` says yes to the Project Upgrade and API Updater prompts.
  - `unity terms accept <version> --yes` accepts the Editor Software Terms without a prompt.
  - `unity install --download-directory <dir>` installs a self-contained Editor into a folder such as a CI workspace.

### Headless
- `unity open --batchmode` starts an Editor with no window. Add `--until-ready` to return once it can take commands:
  ```
  unity open --batchmode --until-ready
  ```
- With `--until-ready`, a blocking dialog (Project Upgrade Required, Script Updating Consent, Enter Safe Mode?, or the Software Terms) fails at once with `OPEN_BLOCKED_BY_DIALOG`. It no longer hangs the script.
- `unity status` reports an Editor stuck at "Enter Safe Mode?" as `STATUS_BLOCKED_BY_DIALOG_SAFE_MODE`. An Editor in Safe Mode fails with `STATUS_SAFE_MODE` and exit code 6.
- `unity logs --console --follow` streams the running Editor's console until you press Ctrl-C.
- **Breaking:** failures that have their own meaning now use their own exit codes instead of 6. For example, 11 means the path isn't a Unity project, or the release or module doesn't exist. Update scripts that check for 6.

content.content:
**Capabilities (from the page)**
- Control the Unity Editor in natural language from any MCP client.
- Create scenes and GameObjects, edit C# scripts, manage assets, run tests, profile, and build.

- Advanced topics with linked guides: multi-instance routing, tool groups (vfx, animation, ui, testing, etc.), Roslyn script validation, and remote-hosted server auth.

**Requirements**
- Unity 2021.3 LTS through 6.x.
- Python 3.10+, installed via `uv`.

**Install and setup**
- Add the package in Unity via Package Manager → Add from git URL, or use `openupm add com.coplaydev.unity-mcp`.
- Run `Window → MCP for Unity → Configure All Detected Clients`.
- The page lists Claude Desktop & Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, and Gemini CLI as supported clients.

**Not covered in the page**
- Specific tools such as read_console, manage_scene, manage_gameobject, run_tests, and screenshot/camera or play mode control are not named or described.
- No Windows-specific setup notes.
- No `claude mcp add` instructions and no comparison of HTTP vs. stdio transport.
- No explicit statement that the Unity Editor must be open, though the tool is built to control the running Editor.

For those details, see the linked tool catalog and the Contributing and Advanced guides.

**Supported Unity versions:** The page doesn't list specific versions. It only links the Editor and Runtime badges to Unity's release archive (unity.com/releases/editor/archive).

**Project path requirement:** "Project path cannot contain spaces." Examples: `C:/MyProjects/MyProject` is valid; `C:/My Projects/MyProject` is not.

**Windows notes:**
- The local server binary sits under `<unityProjectPath>/Library/mcp-server/win-x64/` (also win-x86 and win-arm64).
- If you use Docker on Windows, Docker Desktop must be running first.
- Installation can be done with the `.unitypackage` installer or the CLI.

**Claude Code setup:**
- Claude Code is the recommended agent.
- Easiest route: open `Window/AI Game Developer` in Unity and click "Auto-generate skills."
- CLI route: `npx unity-mcp-cli setup-skills claude-code ./MyUnityProject`.
- Manual route: run `claude mcp add ai-game-developer <command>`, where `<command>` is the binary path with `port` and `client-transport=stdio` for your platform. Replace `<unityProjectPath>` and `<port>`.

**Batchmode, headless, and CI:**
- The page gives one example. It runs Unity with `-batchmode -nographics` and passes `-UNITY_MCP_CLOUD_URL`, `-UNITY_MCP_KEEP_CONNECTED=true`, `-UNITY_MCP_AUTH_OPTION=token`, and `-UNITY_MCP_TOKEN`.
- The CLI has a `wait-for-ready` command for waiting until the editor is ready.
- Command-line overrides apply at runtime. They are written to the config file only on first run or when a new token is generated.
- No further headless guidance is given.

**Cloud vs. local server:**

## Features
- Two-way communication between an AI client and Blender through a socket server
- Create, modify, and delete objects; apply materials and colors
- Visual checks from multiple angles, cameras, wireframe, X-ray, and animation strips, plus renders
- Direct execution of Blender Python written by the AI
- Asset and model generation from several sources (see below)

## Integrations and Costs

| Integration | Cost / Access | Key needed? |
|---|---|---|
| **Poly Haven** | Free; all assets CC0 | No key or account. Tick it in the sidebar. |
| **Poly Pizza** | Free catalogue (~10,600 low-poly models); some models are CC-BY and need credit | Yes, a free key from poly.pizza |
| **Sketchfab** | Listed as a credential option; pricing not stated | Yes (Sketchfab API key) |
| **Meshy** | Via Premium, or your own key on a paid Meshy plan | No with Premium; yes with your own key |
| **Hyper3D Rodin** | Pricing not stated | Yes (Hyper3D API key) |
| **Hunyuan3D** | Pricing not stated; Tencent Cloud account needed | Yes (SecretId/SecretKey) |
| **Tripo** | Pricing not stated | Not specified |
| **Premium** | Lets you generate Meshy, Hunyuan3D, Tripo, and Rodin models without your own keys; price not stated | No |

## Requirements
- Blender 3.0 or newer
- Python 3.10 or newer
- uv package manager

## Install Steps

**Quick option:** run the one-line installer for your OS, or run `uvx mcp-for-blender setup` if you already have uv. The setup installs uv, configures your MCP clients, and enables the addon.

**Manual option:**
1. Install uv using the official installer (not `pip install uv`).
2. Add the server to your MCP client config.
3. Run `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon`.
4. In Blender, go to Edit → Preferences → Add-ons and enable "Interface: MCP for Blender."
5. Press N in the 3D viewport, open the MCP for Blender tab, and click Start MCP Server.

## Claude Code Config

```bash
claude mcp add blender uvx mcp-for-blender
```

## Windows Config
- Install uv with `winget install --id=astral-sh.uv -e`, then open a new terminal.
- In clients such as Cursor, use the command `cmd` with args `["/c", "uvx", "mcp-for-blender"]`. This helps when a GUI-launched client can't find `uvx`, which can cause a `spawn uvx ENOENT` error.
- Fully quit the client from the system tray after config changes.

## Security Warning
The `execute_blender_code` tool can run arbitrary Python inside Blender. The docs say: "ALWAYS save your work before using it." Safe mode (`BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=1`) can check and block risky scripts. The addon's socket server also has no authentication or encryption, so keep it on localhost unless you're on a trusted network.

## Telemetry
- Telemetry is opt-in for content. Prompts, generated code, screenshots, and scene data are collected only if you enable it.
- A minimal anonymous usage record is collected by default.
- To disable all telemetry, set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true`.

**What it is:** The Blender Lab MCP Server is a lightweight Model Context Protocol server that gives a natural language interface to Blender's Python API. It is meant to improve access to documentation and help users explore and understand complex scenes.

**Requirements:**
- Blender 5.1 or newer
- The MCP add-on
- An LLM client
- The MCP server

**Tools:** The page doesn't list specific MCP tools. It describes example uses, including scene analysis for performance bottlenecks, renaming data-blocks, querying data relationships, scene debugging, and documenting geometry nodes setups.

**License:** The page doesn't state a license. It links to Blender's general license page and says the source code is available on the Blender project site.

**Installation:** Blender has no built-in LLM connection, so three external components must be installed and run:
- **Add-on:** Install it by dragging the zip into Blender (twice, to add the Blender Lab repository and then the add-on) or by downloading it and using Install from Disk. This enables update notifications.
- **LLM client:** Follow the llama.cpp documentation or use a client of your choice.
- **MCP server:** Install the `.mcpb` bundle if your client supports it, or install from source using the llama.cpp or setup instructions. The bundle isn't supported by llama.cpp yet.

**Connecting Claude Code:** The page doesn't mention Claude Code. It only covers general MCP-compatible clients and llama.cpp.

**Safety warnings:** The server "will execute LLM generated code in Blender without any guards in place to protect your data." The page recommends using a virtual machine or a system without access to sensitive information.

**What Anthropic funded:** Anthropic joined the Blender Development Fund as a Corporate Patron. The money goes to Blender core development, including foundational work such as the Blender Python API. Blender's press text says, "This support will be dedicated towards Blender core development." The article notes that Blender remains open source, donors don't own the code, and the Blender Foundation still controls planning and review.

**What the Blender connector is:** A Claude connector that gives a natural-language interface to Blender's Python API. Its listed uses are:
- Scene analysis and debugging
- Generating scripts
- Batch-applying changes to objects in a scene

- Claude, since the connector is officially available for it
- Installation instructions hosted by Blender. The article's livestream preview mentions a quick install using the uv package manager.

**How it connects:** The connector is built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for connecting AI models to external data. Anthropic says it is designed to work with other large language models too, not only Claude. The article presents this as a reusable integration layer, though it notes that real-world behavior remains to be seen.

**License:** The article doesn't state a license for the connector. It only says Blender itself stays open source.

The search didn't turn up a Unity 6-specific guide, so the advice below comes from older threads (Blender 2.7x to 4.0 era), and it's worth checking against current Blender and Unity docs.

- **Scale:** The most consistent advice is to set the export's Scale to 1.00 and change Apply Scaling to FBX Units Scale, with Blender's unit system set to meters. One guide reports that this keeps object dimensions intact without rescaling in Unity. Ensure Blenders systems Units is set to Meters and then in the FBX export dialogue, check Scale is set to 1.00, then change Apply Scaling to FBX Units Scale.
- **Transforms first:** Apply rotation and scale in Blender before exporting. One guide warns that objects may still appear incorrectly positioned, scaled and/or rotated if this isn't done.
- **Apply Transform checkbox:** Users disagree on this. One thread says it only works for one generation in the hierarchy, so grandchild transforms can break. Another reports that it seems to work too for rotations.
- **Axes:** Blender's FBX exporter has forward/up settings, and a developer thread notes that Unity added an import option to apply the axis conversion on import. That thread also describes a 180° mismatch when the forward axis is set to -Y. If you set the axis conversion to -Y and +Z the exporter will apply a 180° rotation because it assumes a forward direction of +Y. I didn't find confirmation of the exact "forward -Z, up Y" combination you mentioned, so test it on a cube before exporting a full model.
- **Unity side:** Keep "Preserve Hierarchy" enabled in the model import settings. One user reports that Unity 2017 behaved differently from Unity 5 with one of these workarounds.
- **.blend import:** I found nothing on importing .blend files directly into Unity 6. Exporting to FBX is the path these sources cover.

content.content:
- **VRAM:** About 10 GB for shape generation, 21 GB for texture generation, and 29 GB for shape and texture generation together.
- **OS:** The page says Hunyuan3D 2.1 "supports Macos, Windows, Linux." It doesn't say which of these were tested.
- **License:** The page has no license section or terms, so this can't be determined from the content.
- **Python:** The authors tested with Python 3.10 and PyTorch 2.5.1+cu124.
- **Hunyuan3D 3.0:** The page doesn't mention version 3.0, so I can't say whether it's open-source or API-only. It covers only Hunyuan3D 2.1 and earlier versions.

- **GPU VRAM:** The page says "An NVIDIA GPU with at least 24GB of memory is necessary." It was verified on A100 and H100 GPUs.
- **OS:** The page says "The code is currently tested only on **Linux**." Windows is not mentioned.
- **CUDA and Python:** The recommended CUDA Toolkit is 12.4. The default environment uses PyTorch 2.6.0 with CUDA 12.4. Python 3.8 or higher is required.
- **Attention backend:** The default is flash-attn. GPUs without flash-attn support, such as V100, can use xformers by setting the `ATTN_BACKEND` environment variable.
- **License:** The model and code are released under the MIT License.
- **Dependencies with separate terms:** nvdiffrast and nvdiffrec are governed by their own licenses, which the page links. The page does not describe those terms as non-commercial, so check them directly.
- **Output formats:** The pipeline exports a GLB file (`sample.glb`) with PBR materials and a preview MP4 video. GLB files are exported in OPAQUE mode by default, so transparency requires manually connecting the texture's alpha channel in your 3D software.

**Territory:** The license covers only a defined territory. Section 1.l says the Territory is "the worldwide territory, excluding the territory of the European Union, United Kingdom and South Korea." The opening notice adds that the agreement "DOES NOT APPLY IN THE EUROPEAN UNION, UNITED KINGDOM AND SOUTH KOREA." Section 5(c) states that use outside the Territory is "unlicensed and unauthorized under this Agreement."

**Monthly active user threshold:** Section 4 says that if the monthly active users of Your products or services "is greater than 1 million monthly active users in the preceding calendar month," You must request a license from Tencent. Until Tencent grants that license, You are "not authorized to exercise any of the rights under this Agreement." Tencent decides whether to grant it.

**Restrictions on using outputs to improve other AI models:** Section 5(b) says You must not use the Works or their Output to improve other AI models. The exception is Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.1 itself or its Model Derivatives. Section 1.g adds that Outputs alone are not Model Derivatives. Using the Works to train or distill other models is therefore restricted.

**Commercial use:** The license does not use the word "commercial." Instead:
- The grant in Section 2 is a "non-exclusive, non-transferable and royalty-free limited license."
- Section 1.e defines Licensee as someone using the Works "for any purpose and in any field of use."
- Commercial use is still subject to the 1 million MAU threshold, the Territory limits, and the Acceptable Use Policy (Exhibit A). That policy bars uses such as military purposes (item 19), high-stakes automated decisions (item 14), and unlicensed practice of professions (item 20).

This is a summary of the text provided, not legal advice. I'm not a lawyer, so consult qualified counsel for decisions about your specific use.

The search didn't turn up anything specific to `-batchmode` or `-nographics` in CI, so these are the closest matches.

- **Waiting for end of frame:** A Unity MCP pull request fixed blank play-mode captures by grabbing the texture after the end-of-frame render. It yields `WaitForEndOfFrame`, calls `ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshotAsTexture`, and steps the player loop until the capture completes. The same PR notes that the call returns null from edit-mode scripts. (This change routes the call through a WaitForEndOfFrame coroutine and advances the player loop with EditorApplication.Step() so the captured texture actually contains the composited frame.)
- **Test-runner black screens:** A Unity issue-tracker entry on Oculus says black captures inside a UnityTest broke some graphics tests, and the reporter needed a special-case wait to work around it. (This issue is causing a sub set of the automated graphics tests to fail on Oculus unless I put in a special case wait to work around this.)
- **Known black-image triggers:** Older bugs are linked to DX11 full-screen mode with MSAA at a non-native resolution, where switching off Anti Aliasing in Quality Settings solves the problem (a user report, not an official fix). Another bug reports a black image when Color Space is set to linear and Graphics API for Windows is set to Direct3D11. Both are reported as fixed in older versions.
- **Unity 6 issue:** A Unity 6 (6000.x) report describes dark gray borders in captures when the Game view uses a fixed resolution and the screenshot is taken in play mode. It's a different symptom from a fully black image. (Resize the GameView so that around the rendered image Unity Editor displays dark gray borders.)

Nothing I found confirms that `-nographics` specifically yields blank captures or offers a fix for it. My own understanding is that with no GPU rendering, the capture has nothing to read, so the likely fix is to run tests with a graphics device, for example under a virtual display or a GPU-enabled runner, rather than with `-nographics`. Verify that against Unity's docs before relying on it.

content.content:
**Free for all plans, including Personal:** The post doesn't say.

**Install:** The CLI is a single self-contained binary that adds itself to your PATH. On macOS or Linux, you run a curl install script with `UNITY_CLI_CHANNEL=beta`. On Windows, you run a PowerShell equivalent. Support for package managers like brew, winget, and apt is "coming soon."

**Commands:** The post mentions:
- `unity --help`, `unity install <version> -m <modules>`, `unity editors`, `unity open`, `unity auth login`, `unity modules list`, `unity upgrade`, `unity doctor`
- `unity pipeline install` and `unity pipeline list`
- `unity command`, `unity command eval`, and `unity command eval_file`
- `--format json` or `--format tsv` output, and exit codes 0, 1, and 130

**Agents:** The post presents the CLI as a way for AI agents to work in Unity. Structured output and predictable exit codes give agents parseable results. The Pipeline package lets an agent discover available commands at runtime. `eval` lets an agent inspect a live project and verify its changes.

**GA timing:** The post gives no general availability date. It says the CLI is available now, but describes the Pipeline package as "currently **experimental**." It also includes a safe harbor statement that the roadmap isn't a commitment.

**Requirements:**
- The Pipeline package works with Unity 6.0 LTS and newer.
- The CLI is a standalone binary with no dependencies.
- `eval` is gated behind a security token.
- The runtime API is localhost-only and off by default, intended for dev and QA builds.
- CI can authenticate with a service account through environment variables.

**MCP mode:** The post doesn't describe an MCP mode for the CLI. It mentions MCP only in passing, saying registered commands map onto tools that an MCP server can invoke, and that Unity's own tooling can route through its MCP server.

## Windows installation

The page documents **winget** for Windows. The PowerShell install script is shown only as a tab label, and its command isn't in the provided text, so I can't give you its exact command. Check the "Windows (PowerShell)" tab on the live page for it.

```powershell
winget install Unity.CLI
```

- **Update:** `winget upgrade Unity.CLI`, or `unity self-update`. Winget installs an MSIX package, so `self-update` still works for it.
- **Version output:** winget shows a four-part version (such as `1.0.0.20005`), but `unity --version` reports the full version (such as `1.0.0-beta.5`).
- **Custom location:** Set `UNITY_CLI_HOME` before running the script to install to `<UNITY_CLI_HOME>\bin`.
- **Verify:** Run `unity --version`. If the command isn't found, reopen your terminal or add the install directory to `PATH`.

## Requirements

- **Windows:** Windows 10 21H1 or newer.
- **Other platforms (for reference):** macOS 14 or newer, and Linux RHEL 9 or Ubuntu 22.04 or newer with glibc 2.34+.
- **Hub:** Not required. The CLI can run on machines without Unity Hub, such as headless CI workers.

## Commands

**`unity open`**: Opens a project in the Editor version set in the project's settings.

```powershell
unity open .\MyProject
unity .\MyProject        # "open" can be omitted when the first argument is a path
```

**`unity install` and `unity install-modules`** (related commands from the page):

```powershell
unity install lts
unity install-modules -e 6000.3.7f1 -m ios android
```

**`unity test`, `unity build`, `unity eval`, and `unity mcp`:** The provided content doesn't document these commands. Run `unity --help` or see the [Unity CLI reference](/en-us/unity-cli/unity-cli-reference).

Note that the page says controlling the Editor from the CLI requires the [Unity Pipeline package](/en-us/unity-cli/unity-pipeline/unity-pipeline-package). The page also says to use `unity shell` to run many commands in one interactive session.

## Licensing (Personal)

The provided content doesn't include any licensing note about the Personal plan. See the Unity licensing or Unity Hub documentation for that information.

content.text:
# Unity + Blender под управлением Claude Code без доплат: отчёт на 2026-10-22

**Главный вывод.** Технически всё собирается бесплатно: Unity Personal, Blender, Claude Code и официальный Unity CLI. Но с 30.06.2026 в условиях Unity появился пункт про ИИ-агентов, и он ставит сообщественные MCP-мосты в серую зону. Это самое важное, что я нашёл, и я не ожидал его найти.

## 1. Лицензия Unity в 2026

- **Personal бесплатен**, если выручка и привлечённые средства за 12 месяцев меньше $200K. При превышении нужна подписка. Сборка под Switch, PlayStation и Xbox требует Pro ([Unity Personal](https://unity.com/products/unity-personal)).
- **Runtime Fee отменён** 12.09.2024. Заставка в Unity 6 опциональна. В 2026 Personal остаётся бесплатным; подорожали только Pro и Enterprise ([pricing-updates](https://unity.com/pricing-updates)).
- **Версии.**
  - 6.3 LTS поддерживается до декабря 2027 ([Unity](https://unity.com/releases/unity-6)).
  - 6.0 LTS — до октября 2026.
  - 6.6 (6000.6.0f1) вышла 31.08.2026 ([страница релиза](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/6000.6.0f1)).
  - 6.4 и 6.5 — не LTS и по агрегатору [eosl.date](https://eosl.date/eol/product/unity/) уже сняты с поддержки.
  - Built-in Render Pipeline объявлен устаревшим в 6.5 ([GameFromScratch](https://gamefromscratch.com/unity-6-5-released/)), поэтому для нового проекта берите URP.
  - Рекомендую **6.3 LTS**.
- **Ловушка ToS.** В [Terms of Service](https://unity.com/legal/terms-of-service) от 30.06.2026 пункт 17.2(ff) запрещает обращаться к любому «Offering» через ИИ-агента, CLI или MCP-клиент/сервер «кроме Authorized Agentic Access». «Offering» по определению включает Software, то есть и Editor. Пункт (gg) запрещает сторонние интеграции без письменного разрешения.
- **Что сказал Unity.** Представитель на форуме и в Reddit неформально заявил, что локальная автоматизация ваших файлов допустима. Про управление самим Editor он сказал: «here is where the terms come into play». Применение ограничений приостановлено до проверки сторонних инструментов ([тред](https://discussions.unity.com/t/new-terms-of-service-is-unity-restricting-local-ai-tools-and-ai-training/1724661), [Roboin](https://roboin.io/article/en/2026/07/02/unity-denies-concerns-over-ban-on-third-party-ai/)). Официального списка разрешённых инструментов я не нашёл.
- Это не юридическая консультация. Самый безопасный путь — официальные инструменты Unity (раздел 2).

## 2. Мосты Unity ↔ агент

| Мост | Лицензия и платность | Статус | Возможности |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Unity CLI + пакет Pipeline** (официальный) | Бесплатно, без лимита подключений ([Unity AI](https://unity.com/features/ai)) | Бета, `1.0.0-beta.14` от 21.10.2026 ([release notes](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/release-notes)); пакет экспериментальный | `unity open --batchmode --until-ready`, `eval` (C# в живом Editor), `test`, `build`, `logs --console`, режим `unity mcp`. Windows: `winget install Unity.CLI`, Hub не нужен ([док](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/use-unity-cli)) |
| **[unity-agent-plugin](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/unity-agent-plugin)** (официальный) | Unity Companion License | Бета 0.1.x | Скиллы для Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add Unity-Technologies/unity-agent-plugin`, затем `/plugin install unity@unity-agent-plugin`. Нужен Unity 6+ |
| **[CoplayDev/unity-mcp](https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp)** | MIT, бесплатно | v10.3.0 от 04.10.2026, пуш 19.10.2026, 15.3k звёзд | ~50 инструментов: сцены, GameObject, скрипты, ассеты, тесты, сборка. По сторонним зеркалам: `read_console`, `capture_screenshot` внутри `manage_scene`, управление Editor. Нужны Python 3.10+ и `uv`. Подключение: `Window → MCP for Unity → Configure All Detected Clients` |
| **[IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP)** | Apache-2.0 | Пуш 22.10.2026, 4.5k звёзд | Сцены, GameObject, EditMode/PlayMode тесты, консоль, скриншоты, play mode, Roslyn-выполнение. Подключение: `claude mcp add ... client-transport=stdio`. Путь проекта **не должен содержать пробелов** |
| [CoderGamester/mcp-unity](https://github.com/CoderGamester/mcp-unity) | MIT | Пуш 11.10.2026, ~2k звёзд | Возможности не проверял |

- **justinpbarnett/unity-mcp** теперь тот же репозиторий, что и CoplayDev: GitHub API отдаёт его под именем CoplayDev/unity-mcp.
- **Unity AI / Muse.** Ассистент платный: для Personal пробный период 14 дней, потом $10 в месяц ([Unity](https://unity.com/features/ai), [Vindler](https://vindler.solutions/blog/unity-ai-open-beta)). Он вам не нужен. MCP-сервер Unity по странице Unity бесплатен. Но 20.05.2026 сотрудник писал, что «a subscription is required for an MCP connection» ([тред](https://discussions.unity.com/t/request-for-official-clarification-unity-mcp-access-subscription-requirements-and-future-policy/1720323)). Это противоречие осталось неразрешённым.
- **Известные проблемы Coplay на Windows** ([issues](https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+windows)):
  - `run_tests` ложно падает или зависает при domain reload (#1394);
  - Windows focus-nudge зацикливается (#1407);
  - агента блокирует попап «Reload scene» (#1411);
  - Claude Code показывает «Not Configured» при живом соединении (#1397).
- **Проблемы Unity CLI** ([Vindler](https://vindler.solutions/blog/unity-cli-agent-automation)):
  - токен сбрасывается при входе в Play Mode;
  - модальные окна блокируют агента;
  - ~0.8 с на вызов;
  - скриншотов в CLI нет.

## 3. Headless и верификация без человека

- **Базовые флаги** ([manual](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/EditorCommandLineArguments.html)): `-batchmode -projectPath "..." -executeMethod Класс.Метод -logFile -`. Исключение или ненулевой код выхода дают ненулевой код процесса.
- **Тесты** ([Test Framework](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.test-framework@1.4/manual/reference-command-line.html)): `-runTests -testPlatform EditMode|PlayMode -testResults out.xml`. Результат — NUnit XML.
- **Сборка**: через `BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer` в `-executeMethod` или `unity build`.
- **Скриншоты.** `-nographics` отключает графическое устройство ([manual](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/EditorCommandLineArguments.html)), поэтому для кадров флаг нужно убрать. Нужна реальная видеокарта. Рецепт «дождаться конца кадра, затем ScreenCapture или Camera.Render в RenderTexture» собран из косвенных источников, это не проверенная инструкция. Ждите чёрных кадров и проверяйте на своей конфигурации.
- **Лицензия Personal в batchmode.**
  - Активация из командной строки (`-serial`, `-username`, `-password`) работает только для платных мест. Personal активируется входом в Unity Hub ([doc](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/ManagingYourUnityLicense.html)).
  - На вашей машине после входа в Hub batchmode, по моему предположению, должен работать, но это не задокументировано.
  - Для CI всё хуже: [GameCI](https://game.ci/docs/github/activation) по-прежнему описывает схему с `.ulf`, а [Codemagic](https://help.codemagic.io/articles/2292424011-can-i-make-app-store-builds-using-unity-personal-license-with-codemagic) пишет, что ручная активация Personal больше не поддерживается. Не планируйте облачный CI.
  - Batch mode подпадает под ToS Unity.
- **Дополнительно** (общеизвестное, в этой сессии не проверял): один проект нельзя открыть двумя процессами сразу, то есть Editor и batchmode параллельно не работают.
- **Подсказки из сторонних источников** ([m4bwav/unity-agent](https://github.com/m4bwav/unity-agent), не проверял):
  - Hub CLI из оболочки агента падает, пока не сброшена `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`;
  - быстрая проверка компиляции без Editor — `dotnet build`.
- **Из релиз-нот CLI**: `unity open --batchmode --until-ready` падает сразу с `OPEN_BLOCKED_BY_DIALOG`, а не зависает; `unity terms accept <версия> --yes` принимает условия без диалога.

## 4. Blender ↔ агент

- **Версия.** Сейчас Blender 5.2.3 LTS, следующий — 5.3 в ноябре ([blender.org](https://www.blender.org/download/)).
- **[ahujasid/blender-mcp](https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp)** (теперь «MCP for Blender»):
  - MIT, 32k звёзд, пуш 20.10.2026;
  - Blender 3.0+, нужен запущенный Blender с аддоном (GUI);
  - Claude Code: `claude mcp add blender uvx mcp-for-blender`;
  - есть `execute_blender_code` (произвольный Python), без аутентификации на сокете; телеметрия отключается `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true`.
- **Интеграции.**
  - Poly Haven: бесплатно, CC0, ключ не нужен.
  - Poly Pizza: бесплатный ключ, часть моделей CC-BY.
  - Sketchfab, Hyper3D Rodin, Hunyuan3D (через Tencent Cloud), Tripo, Meshy: нужны свои ключи, цены в README не указаны.
  - «Premium» — платный.
  - Всё это опционально.
- **Официальный сервер Blender Lab** ([blender.org/lab](https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/)): нужен Blender 5.1+, аддон и MCP-сервер (`.mcpb` или установка из исходников). Предупреждение авторов: код от LLM выполняется «без защиты», рекомендуют ВМ. Лицензию страница не называет. Страницу репозитория я не открыл (403).
- **Anthropic.** Компания вступила в Blender Development Fund как корпоративный патрон и выпустила коннектор Claude ([Digital Production](https://digitalproduction.com/2026/04/30/anthropic-funds-blender-ships-claude-connector/)).
- **Что реально нужно.** Для агента без человека MCP не обязателен. Достаточно `blender -b --python gen.py -- аргументы`: стандартные флаги, но страницу мануала целиком открыть не удалось. MCP полезен только для интерактивной отладки.
- **Экспорт в Unity.**
  - Физика Unity ожидает 1 м = 1 единица ([FBX Importer](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/FBXImporter-Model.html)).
  - Вариант A: FBX через `bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx` с `apply_scale_options='FBX_SCALE_ALL'`, `bake_space_transform=True`, forward `-Z`, up `Y`. Параметры у меня по памяти, источники спорят. Проверьте на тестовом кубе.
  - Вариант B: glTF/GLB (Y-up) плюс пакет [glTFast](https://github.com/atteneder/glTFast) (Apache-2.0, его описывают как официальный `com.unity.cloud.gltfast`; полное подтверждение не получено).
  - Перед экспортом применяйте transform и scale.

## 5. Бесплатные ассеты и генерация

- **Безопасные лицензии.** Poly Haven — CC0, коммерческое использование разрешено ([лицензия](https://polyhaven.com/license)). Quaternius утверждён как CC0 в памяти проекта; в этой сессии я его не перепроверял. Kenney — CC0 по общему знанию, тоже не перепроверял. OpenGameArt и Sketchfab смешанные: фильтруйте CC0/CC-BY, красные флаги — GPL, NC, SA. Лицензия Unity Asset Store ограничивает использование движком Unity, не проверял.
- **Ваша видеокарта.** WMI показывает GTX 1660 Ti (поле `AdapterRAM` обрезано до 4 ГБ; сама карта 6 ГБ, это моё знание).
- **[Hunyuan3D 2.1](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1).**
  - [Лицензия](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan3D-2.1/blob/main/LICENSE) Tencent **не действует в ЕС, Великобритании и Южной Корее**. Свыше 1 млн MAU нужно разрешение Tencent, а выходы нельзя использовать для обучения других моделей.
  - Нужно ~10 ГБ VRAM для формы и 21 ГБ для текстуры, 29 ГБ для обоих этапов.
  - Репозиторий не обновлялся с 17.10.2025.
- **[TRELLIS.2](https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS.2).** MIT, пуш 10.07.2026, но нужно ≥24 ГБ VRAM и протестировано только на Linux.
- **Вывод.** Локальная 3D-генерация на 6 ГБ нереалистична. Для текстур локально вручную можно взять [FLUX.1-schnell](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell) (Apache-2.0, 12B параметров, тяжело для 6 ГБ). Проще брать CC0-текстуры и процедурный low-poly через bpy.

## 6. Рекомендуемый конвейер

1. **Человек, один раз:**
   - установить Hub и войти;
   - активировать Personal;
   - поставить Editor 6.3 LTS и принять условия;
   - создать URP-проект по пути без пробелов;
   - установить Unity CLI и пакет Pipeline, подтвердить подключение в Project Settings;
   - поставить Blender.
2. **Агент:** скрипт bpy генерирует модель, делает превью-рендер для самопроверки и экспортирует в `Assets/Models`.
3. **Агент:** C#-скрипты, сцена собирается кодом через `-executeMethod` (детерминированно и под git), EditMode/PlayMode-тесты, XML-результат.
4. **Агент:** скриншот сцены на реальной видеокарте, смотрит и правит. Затем сборка.
5. **Человек всегда:** настройка game feel (прыжок, coyote time, i-frames) руками, оценка картинки глазами, прочтение ToS, подпись билдов.

Практический порядок: основа — `Unity.exe -batchmode` и официальный `unity`-CLI, MCP — по желанию.

## 7. Риски и слабые места

- **Подтверждено источниками:** разрывы связи при domain reload, ложные падения тестов, попапы и фокус на Windows, отсутствие скриншотов в CLI, токены (149 команд CLI ≈ 24k токенов схемы по [m4bwav](https://github.com/m4bwav/unity-agent)).
- **Моя оценка без источников:** агенты плохо судят о красоте и пропорциях без цикла «скриншот → правка», путают ссылки в сериализованных сценах и префабах, галлюцинируют вызовы bpy, а в фоновом режиме Blender часть операторов зависит от контекста.
- **Правовой риск:** пункт 17.2 может ужесточиться, а enforcement «на паузе».
